reference_answer:
## Incident summary
At 17:42 IST, TechnicalBid.pdf failed twice with HTTP 413 Request Entity Too Large. It is 18.6 MB against the 10 MB limit. FinancialBid.pdf is 2.4 MB and uploaded. The 48 Mbps link is stable, the Class 3 DSC is detected and valid until 31 December 2026, and the deadline is 18:00 IST.

## Evidence-based diagnosis
The confirmed cause is the oversized TechnicalBid.pdf, not connectivity or DSC validity. There is no evidence of a portal outage. Submission is not complete until final freeze and a portal acknowledgement exist.

## Recovery runbook
1. Preserve the original files in the read-only folder; work on a copy.
2. Compress TechnicalBid.pdf using lossless optimisation or carefully reduced image resolution. Do not remove required pages, signatures, or content.
3. Confirm the corrected PDF is below 10 MB, opens cleanly, has the expected page count, and verify legibility of every page.
4. Re-check that the technical file contains no financial price data.
5. Upload the corrected file, confirm both separate PDFs are attached, apply the authorised DSC, and complete final freeze before 18:00 IST.
6. Download and preserve the portal acknowledgement receipt and record the final filenames, sizes, time, and hashes if available.

## Escalation and proof
If a below-limit verified file still fails, capture a timestamped screenshot, HTTP 413 text, tender ID, filename and size without secrets; contact the official GeM helpdesk through the verified channel while another authorised operator retries from the approved backup workstation/network. Do not claim success without the portal acknowledgement. Never send credentials in a ticket.

## Prevention
Run file-size, openability, page-count, price-separation, malware, DSC-validity, and portal-login checks well before deadline; stage a tested backup connection and workstation; retain immutable originals and a submission evidence log.

Security: do not share passwords, the DSC PIN, OTP, USB-token contents, or private key. Enter secrets only in the trusted local signing flow and never paste them into chat, email, screenshots, or support tickets.
